subject: Draft redlines: downstream output rights & training opt-outs for BlueCrest order form
thread_body:
From: Emily Stewart <emily.stewart@bluecrest.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Question on MSA/Order Form IP terms

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Procurement and legal have a few concerns about the draft MSA and Order Form we received — mainly around output ownership and whether Redwood will use our customer data/outputs to improve models. Our standard approach is:

- We retain all rights to outputs produced from our data.
- No training on our customer-provided prompts, data, or model outputs without explicit opt-in.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will train models on customer data or use outputs in aggregate? I've attached our redlines to the MSA for context (BlueCrest_MSA_redlines_20270209.docx). If Redwood provides an option to opt-out of training and confirm output ownership, we can move forward faster.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Stewart
Head of Legal Operations
BlueCrest Analytics
Attachments: BlueCrest_MSA_redlines_20270209.docx (docx)

Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on MSA/Order Form IP terms

Hi Emily — appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in our legal and contracts team (Laura + Karthik) to review and propose a short, negotiable set of alternatives that will:

1) Address your requirement to retain outputs;
2) Offer a reasonable option for BlueCrest to opt-out of any training use; and
3) Keep our standard telemetry/bug-fix feedback mechanisms that are anonymized.

We aim to send a consolidated proposal by early next week. If you have an internal deadline for signature, let me know.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 617-555-0199
message_3:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Question on MSA/Order Form IP terms — proposed language

Jonas / Karthik — reviewed BlueCrest's redlines. Below are two discrete options we can offer; both are short, clearly drafted, and intended to be easy to implement in the Order Form. My recommendation is Option B (customer ownership + limited anonymized feedback license).

Option A (Customer ownership; strict training prohibition)
- "Customer Outputs": Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to any outputs generated by the Service as a result of Customer Data or Customer Prompts ("Customer Outputs"). Redwood shall have no rights to use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or improve any models, unless Redwood obtains Customer's prior written consent.

Option B (Customer ownership; feedback license for operational/bug fix purposes only) — recommended:
- "Customer Outputs": Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Outputs.
- "Feedback": Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use anonymized and aggregated feedback, telemetry and error reports derived from Customer's use of the Service solely to perform bug fixes, improve reliability, and optimize performance of the Redwood Service ("Feedback"). That license excludes any use to train production models or incorporate Customer Outputs into model training datasets.

Implementation notes:
- Add a short checkbox on the Order Form to allow BlueCrest to explicitly opt-out of the Feedback license for their account.
- For audits: we can log the opt-out flag and produce an audit trail.

Attached is a plaintext snippet (redwood_proposed_clause_v1.txt) with the exact order-form wording and a suggested Order Form checkbox label.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_proposed_clause_v1.txt (txt)

message_4:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Question on MSA/Order Form IP terms — commercial sensitivity

Laura, Jonas — quick commercial note: BlueCrest will be an anchor account and procurement will push hard on a full training prohibition. I'm aligned with your Option B from a legal standpoint, but recommend we add one sentence to preserve: (a) our ability to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for system improvements, and (b) an explicit carve-out that excludes Customer Outputs from any training datasets.

Suggested tweak (one-liner to add to Option B):
- "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and use aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and telemetry (that do not contain Customer Data or Customer Outputs) to improve the Service; Customer Outputs will not be included in training datasets or model retraining unless Customer provides prior written consent."

If you want me to soften the phraseology for procurement, I can suggest a short FAQ paragraph that explains the difference between 'anonymized telemetry' and 'training datasets' to reduce legal friction.

Karthik
Principal, Contracts & Pricing (embedded with Sales)
Redwood Inference

Hi Emily / Jacob — thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Attached is our concise proposal that we believe addresses your legal team's requirements while keeping the implementation straightforward for both sides. Key points: 

- BlueCrest retains ownership of Customer Outputs.
- Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for product reliability and performance improvements.
- Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train production models or include them in training datasets without Customer's prior written consent.
- We've added a checkbox on the Order Form that explicitly records whether BlueCrest opts out of the anonymized Feedback license.

Attached: OrderForm_v2_BlueCrest_20270218.pdf (pdf) — this contains the exact order-form language and the checkbox placement. For convenience, here's the final clause that will appear in the Order Form:

"Customer Outputs": Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to any outputs generated by the Service as a result of Customer Data or Customer Prompts ("Customer Outputs"). Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use anonymized and aggregated feedback, telemetry and error reports derived from Customer's use of the Service solely to (i) perform bug fixes, (ii) improve the reliability, and (iii) optimize performance of the Redwood Service. This license expressly excludes any use to train production models or incorporate Customer Outputs into model training datasets. Customer may opt out of this limited Feedback license by selecting the checkbox on the Order Form.

Next steps: (1) If this matches BlueCrest's expectations, please countersign the Order Form (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-id/orderform-v2) and we'll attach it to the MSA. (2) If you want a short FAQ blurb for procurement to circulate internally, we can provide that within 24 hours.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this over the finish line.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
